verdicts.reason: The two absorbing states give distinct bounded solutions v₀ and v₁, and starting at b never hits A. The proof and dependency restatements are consistent with the supplied interfaces.

The cited sphere interfaces establish the antipode as a minimizing conjugate endpoint. The explicit unit directions are distinct, and their initial velocities give infinitely many distinct minimizing geodesics. No fatal defect found.
The curvature, Chern-form normalization, Hermitian compatibility, and exact primitive all follow from the cited interfaces. The unequal closed forms therefore represent the same real de Rham class.
F10 inaccurately restates its dependency: only polynomial algebras in finitely many variables are finitely presented. For example, k[x₁,x₂,…] is not finitely presented over k.

The proof establishes s∉k^p, applies the supplied general theorem with its exact hypotheses, and verifies that L/k is purely inseparable. The base-change and local-ring claims match the dependency interfaces.
The localization and fibre computations follow from the cited interfaces. The canonical map k[t]_(t)→k has nonzero kernel (t)k[t]_(t), so this example refutes the universal claim.
The zero curvature form has integral zero, and the cited Gauss–Bonnet theorem then gives 2πχ(M)=0. The hypotheses and dependency restatements match the supplied interfaces.

The nonempty hypothesis makes K dA a nonzero, nonnegative compactly supported top form. The cited positivity result gives a positive integral, and global Gauss–Bonnet then gives χ(M)>0. The dependency restatements and choice assumption match their interfaces.

The proof establishes the stated isomorphism using coherent cohomology, field base change, and the structure of reduced connected finite-dimensional algebras. The inseparable example supports the sharpness claim; no fatal defect found.

The cited perfect-complex interface supplies fibrewise cohomology; rank-nullity gives its Euler characteristic as the alternating sum of term dimensions, which are locally constant for finite projective modules. The hypotheses and edge cases are covered.

The parent theorem covers the stated smooth-boundary presentations and explicitly makes the corner sum empty. The proof correctly specializes its formula, including the boundaryless case; the dependency restatements support the steps used.
The cited interfaces support the construction of smooth affine opens and the tangent-space criterion; density of closed points extends smoothness to every scheme point. No fatal defect found.

The cited interfaces support the tangent-dimension bound, existence of a regular closed point, and propagation of regularity through automorphisms and localization. The equivalence and transitive-space claim follow.
The Green identity gives zero gradient on each component for n≥2; the interval argument covers n=1. The stated hypotheses and dependency interfaces support both cases.
The classification theorem explicitly states the biconditional. Its canonical polygonal models support the genus and crosscap Euler counts used in the proof; no fatal defect found.

The proof supports both cases: Bertini and dimension drop produce a good tuple, while the closed rank-defect locus gives an open set of smooth, pure-dimensional intersections. The cited interfaces and boundary cases are consistent.

The proof correctly reduces fibre cohomology to a finite projective complex. Locally constant term dimensions and upper semicontinuity of cokernel fibre dimensions give lower semicontinuity of differential ranks, hence upper semicontinuity of cohomology dimensions.

The graph limits follow from the cited weak-stability lemma. Both counterexample sequences converge in the stated norms, while their limits lack the required transverse derivative. No fatal defect found.

The final remark says [[thm-serre-criterion-ampleness]] proves a cohomological characterisation of ampleness, but its supplied interface states only a global-generation criterion. That citation does not support the page promise.

The positive-return argument follows from irreducibility and Chapman–Kolmogorov, and the cited period lemma makes the chain period well-defined. The stated edge cases are consistent with the definition.
The cell intersections, local face charts, and vertex links give the stated triangulation. The dependency restatements and boundary conventions are consistent; no fatal defect found.

The construction establishes measurable, square-integrable operations, a well-defined finite pairing on almost-everywhere classes, and the inner-product axioms. The stated boundary cases and supplied interfaces are consistent.
The definition matches the supplied smoothness and relative-dimension interfaces; the pointwise conditions, edge cases, and examples are consistent.
The definition and its consequences follow from the supplied flatness and fpqc interfaces. Target-locality, empty cases, and open-cover examples are consistent.

The evaluation map, stalkwise criterion, and finite-generation argument for invertible sheaves on quasi-compact schemes are valid. The dependency restatements and ampleness remark are consistent with the supplied interfaces.

The chart-independence argument is valid. Connectedness and the standard identity theorem ensure that a nonconstant sphere-valued holomorphic map has isolated poles, giving the claimed agreement with the plane-domain definition.
The polarization, adjoint invariance, infinitesimal identity, determinant example, and Pfaffian transformation are valid under the stated real and complex conventions, including degree zero.

The one-point example omits e_0, although indices start at 0. Taking e_0=1 and a≠0 satisfies its stated data but gives a nonzero matrix coefficient at (0,0), contradicting the claim that all coefficients except (1,1) vanish.

F5 overstates its cited primitive corollary: that interface guarantees a primitive only on some neighbourhood of each point, not on an entire disc. The stronger dependency restatement is unsupported, even though step 4.1 needs only a local primitive.

The cited counting formula, First Main Theorem, and Ahlfors–Shimizu identity justify eventual positivity, monotonicity, and the stated range of both orders. The dependency restatements and A/B interfaces are consistent.

The local link condition, closed quotient relation, compactness, Hausdorffness, second countability, and finite cell counts are consistent with the stated dependencies and paired surface models. No fatal defect found.
The construction, tautological quotient, rank-zero case, quotient convention, and base-change claim agree with the supplied interfaces. No fatal defect found.
The equations, canonicalization, tensor flattening, oracle tables, and zero-dimensional cases are consistent with the supplied dependency interfaces.

The claimed equivalence for pure relative dimension drops smoothness. Spec(k[ε]/(ε²))→Spec(k) has a geometric fibre of local dimension 0 at every point, but is not smooth, so it does not meet the stated definition.

The “No finiteness” remark incorrectly says finite generation is needed for the relative invertibility of twists. The cited theorem requires generation in degree one, with no finite-generation hypothesis; the same condition works on affine charts.

The definition makes a Riemann surface a space X that merely admits an atlas, without including the atlas as part of the object. On X=ℂ, the charts z and conjugate(z) give incompatible atlases, so “the complex structure of X” is not determined.
The shift matches the dependency’s twist. Composition, inverse, degree-map functoriality, and homogeneous localization follow with the stated gradings.

The bialternant quotient is integral, symmetric, and homogeneous, and the specialization argument establishes compatibility at every rank, including the boundary and rank zero. The cited dependency interfaces match its use.
The openness and basis arguments follow from the supplied Proj topology and primeness. The nilpotence remark matches the stated finite-generation hypothesis.

The definitions are well typed and consistent with the supplied dependencies. Invariance by equality, strong continuity, intertwiners, equivalence, and the commutant are stated correctly; no fatal defect found.

The Choice accounting contradicts a cited dependency: the affine quasi-coherent equivalence explicitly uses AC for compactness of Spec A as well as for associated-sheaf results, but this item says its only AC use is inherited from associated-sheaf machinery.
The domain and tempered extension are well defined, and the translation identity follows with the stated Fourier signs. The cited dependency interfaces support each step; no fatal defect found.

The quasi-compactness remark reverses the implication: a quasi-compact X over a quasi-compact S need not have a quasi-compact structure morphism. Glue two copies of Spec k[x₁,x₂,…] along ⋃ᵢD(xᵢ); either chart’s inclusion is a counterexample.
The definition agrees with both dependency interfaces, including the zero-dimensional case and the normalized distance formula. No fatal defect found.
The two integrations by parts give 2φ(0). The cited first-derivative and injectivity interfaces support the Sobolev conclusions, and the dependency restatements match the supplied interfaces.

The barriers establish regularity of both circles, and uniqueness of the continuous harmonic extension gives the stated masses. The compactness argument works by taking an open neighbourhood inside each given neighbourhood.
The atlas checks, topological properties, and annulus path argument are valid. The omitted openness checks for the disc and annulus are routine; no fatal defect found.

F5 asserts that every twist is invertible, but its cited twisting-sheaf definition explicitly does not establish this. The needed standard-graded invertibility theorem is neither a dependency nor proved here, leaving coherence and the use of χ in 1.1 unjustified.

The cited initial-ideal and Jacobian results give the doubled cone and two-dimensional tangent space. The proof correctly shows that y is nonzero and nilpotent in the cone ring, and that the reduced cone is the x-axis.
The minors, fibre dimensions, vanishing loci, and nonfreeness argument are correct and supported by the cited interfaces. No fatal defect found.
Accepted. The flatness arguments match the supplied comparison and transgression interfaces, and the genus-two flat plane bundle has Euler number −1 by the cited construction.

The translation charts define a closed oriented flat metric; the 3×3 periodic triangulation has V=9, E=27, F=18. The cited curvature and Euler-characteristic results support K=0, χ(T²)=0, and Gauss–Bonnet.
The metric, connection form, curvature, area integral, and octahedral Euler characteristic are consistent with the cited interfaces. The boundary and continuity arguments are standard.
The multiplier bounds, semigroup laws, strong L² derivatives, and distributional PDE identities follow from the cited interfaces. No fatal defect found.
The proof correctly applies the supplied cohomology and counting results, and its case split covers every integer twist, including n=0 and the boundary values.
[F3] inaccurately restates def-division-ring by omitting its required axiom 1≠0. Its stated condition holds vacuously for the zero ring, which the dependency explicitly excludes.

Step 2.2 invokes a disk-region hypothesis absent from the statement. Compactness alone does not ensure the nondegenerate regular disk and three embedded sides required by F4. Collinear vertices give zero area, defeating the claimed strict inequality.

The crosscap move takes the Klein bottle word to aabb. The corner identifications give one vertex, the paired seam reverses orientation, and the cell count gives Euler characteristic 0. The dependency and A/B interfaces are consistent.

The weighted Fourier criterion reduces membership to integrability of (1+|ξ|²)^s. The polar and block comparisons correctly give convergence exactly when 2s+n<0; the endpoint has logarithmic divergence. No fatal defect found.
The radiality argument, divergence theorem calculation, integration at the origin, and convergence estimates are valid under the stated hypotheses and supplied dependencies.

The multiplicity, Jacobian kernel, and scheme-theoretic tangent cone follow from the cited interfaces. In characteristic other than 2, the leading form has two distinct linear factors, each occurring once.
The free-module flatness, empty-equation Jacobian chart, relative dimension, and n=0 étaleness follow from the supplied interfaces under the stated choice assumption.
The chart calculations establish holomorphy and all ramification indices; the degree and Riemann–Hurwitz count follow from the cited interfaces. No fatal defect found.
The quotient identification, cell count, and orientation-reversing seam argument are valid; the dependency restatements and A/B interfaces are consistent.

Step 1.1 assumes the root homomorphism is the identity on SL₂, but the cited interface does not fix that normalization. For the allowed homomorphism φ=Ad(diag(2,1/2)), u₋α(z)e₁=e₁+(z/4)e₂, so the claimed chart coordinate t=z is false.
The chart equations are squarefree, their gradients never vanish on the quadric, and the cited dimension, Jacobian, regularity, and smoothness results support all stated conclusions.

The affine coordinate has the claimed weak derivatives, and the cited Sobolev positive-part and truncation rules give the stated function and gradient for every 1≤p≤∞. The interface sets are null. No fatal defect found.
The quotient construction, cell count, homeomorphism to the two-hemisphere sphere, and orientability argument follow from the cited interfaces. No fatal defect found.

F3 falsely claims that morphisms Spec D→X correspond to maps from a coordinate ring for arbitrary k-schemes X. For X=P¹ₖ, global functions are k, but there are many D-points. The cited definition does not license this restatement.

The Fourier identities, Schwartz-domain claims, and high-frequency bump argument follow from the supplied interfaces. They establish the translation isometry and rule out a bounded L² extension of differentiation.

The Cayley kernel identity, normalization, compact-support representation, local uniform limit, and boundary estimate are valid. The two-sided integral follows by applying the cited half-line result to each tail.

The gluing defines a flat rank-two bundle and the stated extension. The fibrewise Laurent-polynomial calculation gives h⁰=1 exactly where a vanishes, namely at (a), and h⁰=0 elsewhere. No fatal defect found.
The kernel calculation, factorial power bound, resolvent argument, and trace-class conclusion follow from the cited interfaces. No fatal defect found.

The spherical octant has three great-circle geodesic sides and three intrinsic right angles, giving angle sum 3π/2. The cited dependency interfaces support the proof and the supplementary Gauss–Bonnet check.
The Euclidean-line example is a valid counterexample: γ(t)=t is an affine geodesic, its curvature vanishes, and J(t)=t²∂x has D_t²J=2∂x≠0. The dependency restatements and edge cases are consistent.

The fat Cantor set is a closed, nowhere dense, nonnull witness, so it refutes the claimed implication. The cut-locus volume statement and local dependency restatements agree with the supplied interfaces.

The coefficient-space construction is valid, the antipode converts the left coaction to a group representation with coefficients that generate A, and the cited quotient-spectrum theorem yields the claimed closed immersion.
The chart, local barrier, boundary regularity, and odd reflection steps are valid under the cited interfaces. The reflected Green kernel gives the claimed C² extensions and zero boundary trace.

The construction gives nested connected components of regular polynomial superlevel sets, with compact closures inside Ω and eventual containment of every compact subset. The reuse of P_{j+1} for paths and a polynomial is a notation slip, but its intended meanings are clear.
The multiplier transfers, norm bounds, inverse maps, inclusion, derivative estimate, and nonisometry witness follow from the cited interfaces. No fatal defect found.

The proof correctly uses the generic-point chart and the function-field isomorphism to clear finitely many denominators. The resulting localization map is an isomorphism, and the claimed principal-open restriction follows.

The shifted-kernel argument justifies smooth parameter differentiation, and Cauchy–Pompeiu gives the claimed ∂̄ identity with the stated sign. The other-coordinate identities follow by differentiation under the integral.
The pushout, finite type and quasi-separatedness checks, and valuative existence and uniqueness follow from the supplied interfaces. No fatal defect found.

The proof establishes Noetherianity, uniqueness of generic points, and the dimension-one bound needed to show every proper irreducible closed subset is a single closed point. The dependency restatements and edge cases check out.
The proof’s localization, rank detection, regular-element choice, and induction through the quotient all follow from the supplied dependencies. No fatal defect found.

F2 inaccurately restates its dependency: the equivalence covers integral finite-type schemes satisfying the affine-overlap separation condition, not all integral finite-type schemes. The affine line with doubled origin is a counterexample.
The pointwise and global claims follow from smoothness stability, additivity of relative dimension, and the canonical fibre isomorphism. The cited dependency interfaces are consistent with the proof.
The lifting, determinantal, and regular-sequence arguments establish an open neighbourhood of each exact fibre point. The dependency uses and edge cases check out; no fatal defect found.
The proof establishes a finite chartwise cellulation and compatible topological refinement. Its dependency restatements, edge handling, and avoidance of F are consistent with the supplied interfaces.
The cited interfaces support the proof. The affine base-change calculation and finite-generator argument are valid; composition follows directly from the definition without AC.
The construction and quotient map establish a one-polygon schema homeomorphic to S. The dependency restatements, regularity hypotheses, and A/B interfaces are consistent; no fatal defect found.

The CP¹ period and Thom-class sign agree, and the finite projective factorization around each compact cycle extends the equality to M. The connection comparison and edge cases are supported by the cited interfaces.

The kernel comparison via finite lifts and shears proves presentation independence. The determinant and augmentation identities support the comparison, and right exactness gives base change. Negative indices are covered by the stated convention.
Each proof step follows from the cited facts. The dependency restatements match their interfaces, and the hypotheses cover the local ring and scheme cases.

The filtration, stabilization of kernels, induction on algebra generators, and splitting after localisation are valid under AC. The dependency restatements match the supplied interfaces; no fatal defect found.

The finite surjection, coherent kernel, high-twist H¹ vanishing, and shifted polynomial-tail argument establish finite generation. The closed-subscheme case follows by coherent pushforward and the projection formula; the stated edge cases are covered.

The local equations glue consistently, elimination of an invertible section gives the claimed projective bundle charts, fibres recover the zero schemes, and those charts establish smoothness. No fatal defect found.

The normalization argument produces a quasi-finite polynomial map near the point. The cited finite factorization then bounds every fibre’s Krull dimension by n, giving the claimed local bound. No fatal defect found.

The Jacobi-field argument establishes invertibility along the segment; the local inverse branches glue, and the Gauss-lemma comparison and equality case follow. The dependency restatements match the supplied interfaces.
The gap recurrence, initial 1/m bound, edge-growth induction, and satisfiability induction follow from the supplied interfaces. The m=1 and edgeless cases cause no defect.
Step 6.1 falsely says Countable Choice is used only through F2–F4. The proof also invokes F6, F7, and the Lebesgue-measure part of F8, whose supplied interfaces explicitly assume it.
The fiber cohomology calculation, Leray–Hirsch injection, properness, and rank-zero through rank-two cases check out against the supplied interfaces. No fatal defect found.

The ear induction proves the facial-cycle claim; Alexander duality gives the face count, and the bipartite bound and facewise Schönflies extension follow. The cited dependency interfaces support the steps used.

The local analytic arguments yield finitely many slab graphs with Puiseux endpoints. The band fans and pinched-band construction give graph-bounded triangles, and wall marks make their intersections face to face. No fatal defect found.

The cited interfaces support the steps used. The grid and parity argument establishes polygonal connectivity of the arc complement, and the first-exit construction gives accessible points dense in the component frontier.
The cut, subdivision, and merge steps preserve the quotient; the displayed word identities and stated edge cases check out against the supplied interfaces.

The finite line-bundle presentation and both descending inductions follow from the cited interfaces. The closed-immersion clause uses the standard local projection-formula identification; the stated edge cases are covered.

The construction gives a quasi-coherent homogeneous ideal whose affine restrictions are the unique saturated ideals of the closed subscheme; the local quotient Proj presentations glue. The cited interfaces support each step.

The affine charts give finite-type ring maps, their finite cover makes each affine-base preimage quasi-compact, and the cited local criteria yield finite type. The empty-base and n=0 cases are covered.
The cited Čech computation and cup-product naturality justify Laurent multiplication. The monomial bases are dual, and polynomial compatibility follows. No fatal defect found.

The Čech complex has flat terms and computes cohomology after arbitrary base change. The descending finite free replacement and Tor argument justify the bounded finite projective truncation. No fatal defect found.

The coordinate-change law gives a well-defined pullback, and the local form w=z^e yields coefficient e z^{ek+e-1}u(z^e), with a nonzero holomorphic unit. The order formula and stated special cases follow.

The comparison map is well defined on distinguished opens, becomes the standard base-change isomorphism on stalks, and the resulting affine charts cover X. Dependency restatements and edge cases are consistent.
The local Koszul resolutions, dual-complex calculation, adjunction identification, and transition maps support the stated sheaf Ext isomorphism and its naturality.

The injective acyclicity argument supports the local-to-global spectral sequence; the cited sheaf Ext concentration collapses it to the claimed groups. The stated sign is explicitly applied once, and the edge cases are covered.
The affine restriction and Proj chart computations are valid; naturality of tensor products and localization gives the stated compatibility and cocycle, so the gluing conclusion follows.

Each nonzero element survives at an associated-prime localization. An associated-prime witness remains nonzero after localization and is annihilated by the maximal ideal, giving depth zero. The dependency and choice assumptions suffice.

The extension-by-zero modules represent sections, their coproduct is a generator, filtered colimits are stalkwise exact, and the cited embedding theorem yields the stated resolution. No fatal defect found.
The affine localization argument establishes quasi-coherence, and the cited closed-subscheme correspondence and agreement criterion support the remaining claims. The empty cases are covered.

The rank-one decomposition, root conjugation, double-coset argument, closure and dimension proof, and two-chart quotient construction are consistent with the supplied dependencies. No fatal defect found.
The stabilizer, closed-orbit, fibre, dimension, and smoothness arguments follow from the supplied interfaces. No fatal defect found.

The transverse hyperplane slices reduce the tangent space to the line kv while preserving smoothness and local dimension. The zero-vector and dimension-boundary cases are handled. F20 has a minor indexing inconsistency, but the proof uses the stated one-based relabeling.

Each clause follows from base-change stability of smoothness; the pointwise clause follows by applying that argument on a smooth neighbourhood of x. The dependency restatements and empty-fibre case are consistent.
The pasting argument correctly establishes the weak derivative identities, uniqueness, and both norm bounds. The dependency interfaces support the steps, including the empty-domain case.

The flat base change annihilator calculation, Noether normalization comparison, and finite open cover dimension argument are valid. The dependency restatements and edge cases are consistent with the supplied interfaces.
The affine universal-property argument gives a graded base-change isomorphism; its compatibility lets the restriction and pullback maps glue. The stated hypotheses and edge cases are covered.
The affine comparison map is well defined and stalkwise an isomorphism. The affine-open restriction lemma supplies common affine charts, so the affine cover criterion proves quasi-coherence.

The dependency restatements match their interfaces. AC supplies HB and Countable Choice, and the weak lower semicontinuity corollary applies to the Sobolev normed space and its weakly convergent sequence.

The conjugate-point definition and index-form integration by parts prove (a). On the sphere, the meridian construction, length bound, and Jacobi-field calculation establish all claims in (b); the cited interfaces support the proof.

The title claims the gradient identity off the cut locus, which includes p. In positive dimension, distance from p is not differentiable at p, so its gradient is undefined there. The proof only covers points outside {p}∪Cut(p).

Each arc follows from the tangent-angle formula; summing gives the first identity. The corner definition extends consistently, and the rotation law cancels frame changes on each subarc. No fatal defect found.

The claim that equal fibre dimensions require surjectivity is false. Over A=k[a,b]/(ab), take the same P¹ extension with class a. At s=(a,b), (f_*E)(s) and H⁰(E_s) both have dimension 1, but the base-change map is zero.
The mathematical claims agree with the supplied dependency interfaces; the Jacobian, tangent-cone, dual-number, and regularity qualifications are correctly scoped.

The projective-line example is proper, the infinite direct sum is quasi-coherent but not of finite type, and its global sections form an infinite-dimensional k-vector space. The cited interfaces support the argument.
The closed-surface identity matches its dependency. The remarks about classification and higher-dimensional Gauss–Bonnet accurately describe the theorem’s scope; no fatal defect found.

The proof’s cutoff, mollification, summable line convergence, and Fubini steps establish one measurable ACL representative with the stated weak derivatives. The dependency restatements support the cited uses; no fatal defect found.
The affine-open acyclicity argument correctly gives zero stalks for each positive higher direct image. The dependency interfaces support the steps, and the stated edge cases introduce no defect.

Step 1.1 applies the binary conversion without establishing its hypothesis: it requires every constraint to have arity at least one, while the tester and composition interfaces guarantee only arity at most six and allow zero-arity constraints.

The fibre functor, local construction of morphisms, evaluation isomorphism, and character classification follow from the cited torsor charts and character restriction. The sign convention is consistent.

The affine-overlap criterion makes every finite cover intersection affine; quasi-coherence restricts to each intersection, affine acyclicity applies, and Leray gives the comparison. The stated empty-cover cases are consistent with the interfaces.

The proof reduces each claim to finite generation over Noetherian affine charts. The cited interfaces support the reductions, and the kernel, image, cokernel, extension, and direct-sum arguments follow.
The affine reduction, finite-free criterion, and naturality comparisons support all three conclusions. The dependency restatements and stated edge cases reveal no fatal defect.

[A1] says ACω enters only through the exponential-map definition and Jacobi-field differential theorem. But step 5.1 also invokes the openness/smoothness theorem, and step 6.1 invokes the differential-at-zero theorem; both explicitly assume ACω. The choice audit misstates its dep
The proof follows the stated BLR, tensor, and subsum bounds. Canonicalization preserves the quadratic forms; the soundness cases, resource counts, and dimension-zero edge cases check out.
Step 6.1 indexes balls B(q,1/n) by all n∈ℕ, but 0∈ℕ, so the first radius is undefined. The cited sequential-closure interface explicitly uses 1/(n+1); the stated choice audit is invalid as written.

The standard smooth chart gives a Jacobian presentation whose invertible minor makes Ω free of rank m−c. The cited fibre result identifies m−c with the stated relative dimension, including after field extension.
The proof follows from the cited smoothness and flat–unramified equivalences; the additional derivation argument correctly establishes uniqueness of square-zero lifts. No fatal defect found.

The proof correctly uses the cited Jacobian criterion to obtain a standard smooth chart of relative dimension zero around each étale point. The same chart works throughout its principal open, proving openness and étaleness of the restriction.

The proof correctly reduces each étale stalk to k, splits finite type affine charts into finite products of k, and uses quasi-compactness to obtain the global finite decomposition. The converse and infinite-union example also check out.
The proof establishes openness, local invertibility, injectivity, surjectivity, and smoothness of the inverse. The dependency restatements and edge cases are consistent with the supplied interfaces.

The stalk computation and local flatness show that tensoring with each stalk O_{X,x} detects nonzero O_{S,s}-modules. Surjectivity supplies an x over each s, and stalkwise vanishing then gives F=0. The dependency restatements and edge cases are sound.

Step 4.1 claims [F2] yields triangular faces, but its supplied interface guarantees only Jordan-disk faces. The asserted fan construction and positive sectors are absent from that interface. Steps 5–8 depend on those stronger claims, so the triangulation is not established.

The finite triangulation and local summation interfaces yield the stated formula in case (a). The metric extension and collar charts make case (b) a regular oriented region, and the Euler characteristic interfaces identify the cell counts.

The cited generic freeness lemma applies to each finite type affine chart. A common nonzero localization for each finite cover makes the restricted charts flat, and flatness then holds over their dense open union.

The proof follows from the supplied critical-locus bound and tangent criterion; the passage from closed points to all scheme points and the fibre arguments are valid for finite-type schemes over k. No fatal defect found.
The cited interfaces support the proof steps. The representation, bounded-Laplacian hypothesis, and boundary density formula have consistent signs and sufficient regularity.
Step 2.1 establishes the pole corrector only on a disc around a. The cited Green-function definition requires a harmonic corrector on all of Ω, so the proof has not shown that −log|φ| is a candidate.
The endpoint bounds, interpolation, and identification of the extension with the Fourier coefficient map follow from the cited interfaces. No fatal defect found.

The induction uses the cited hyperplane lemma and Euler characteristic additivity correctly; field extension preserves every twisted Euler characteristic, and Serre vanishing gives eventual equality with the Hilbert function.

The induction follows from the cited hyperplane lemma, Euler-characteristic additivity, eventual global generation, and field-extension results. The dependency restatements and boundary cases are consistent with their interfaces.

The finite-presentation hypothesis permits the pointwise criterion, and the cited standard-smooth results establish the converse and dimension claim. Dependency restatements and edge cases are consistent.

The stalkwise affine argument identifies kernels, images, and cokernels with associated module sheaves; the affine-cover and biproduct steps then establish the abelian subcategory and exact embedding without quasi-separatedness. Dependencies are used consistently.

The proof meets the Grothendieck spectral sequence hypotheses. Its filtration and edge maps follow from the supplied theorem, and the module comparison via flasque resolutions is valid (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01EY).

The ratios define compatible chart maps; the transition rules glue both the morphism and the pullback isomorphism. Uniqueness and the empty and vanishing-section cases follow from the stated hypotheses.
The proof establishes a local free chart at every free stalk using finite presentation to kill the finitely generated kernel. The rank-zero case and the fibre-dimension counterexample are sound.
The Green identity signs, unit flux, vanishing boundary term, limit at the pole, and translation step are consistent with the supplied interfaces. No fatal defect found.

The divisor counts are finite, the logarithmic singularities have finite continuous circular means, and the integrated-count identity and nonmonotonicity example are valid. Dependency restatements and A/B interfaces are consistent.
The cutoff limits, boundary-flux sign, cancellation formula, Hölder estimate, and distributional-to-pointwise step follow from the stated dependencies. No fatal defect found.

The Tonelli bound gives local integrability, Fubini and the point-source identity give the distributional equation, and uniform derivative bounds establish smooth harmonicity off the support. The dependency uses and edge cases check out.

The local logarithmic correction is harmonic near the pole and patches with the corrector’s harmonicity away from it. Both pullbacks are candidates, so leastness gives the two inequalities and hence equality.

The Blaschke factors cancel each interior divisor with the stated sign, leaving a zero-free holomorphic function whose logarithmic modulus is harmonic. Poisson representation and the regular-radius limit justify the formula.

The vertex-reduction split/merge preserves the schema and shortens the chosen vertex class. Subsequent extractions reduce the unprocessed pair count; the digon and mixed cases are covered. No fatal defect found.
The degree-zero charts, overlap localizations, and transition formulas agree with the supplied interfaces. Gluing gives the stated canonical isomorphism, including base change and n=0.
The cited local normal form, properness, and connectedness support finite fibres, a constant weighted count, locally finite branch values, and the covering claim. No fatal defect found.

The distinguished opens satisfy the cited cofinal-basis lemma’s hypotheses. The affine equivalence identifies Čech sections with the localizations in the exact unit-ideal complex, including the empty and zero cases.
The equivalence follows from the definition and affine comparison theorem. The restriction isomorphism and naturality give the stated commuting square, including the empty case.

The proof establishes the field extension, regularity of Spec L, and a nonregular local ring after base change to L. The dependency restatements and stated edge cases are consistent with the supplied interfaces.
The cited interfaces supply the nonzero-rank orbit and torsor claims. The proof handles rank zero directly, and the quotient argument follows from the stated Zariski-local product charts.

The proof establishes the pairing’s naturality, proves the degree-zero case from twisting sheaves and presentations, then uses compatible connecting maps and negative-twist presentations for all higher degrees. Finiteness gives perfectness.

The proof correctly obtains a very ample power, applies uniform projective-space vanishing to finitely many coherent pushforwards, and covers every large twist by residue classes. The cited interfaces support each step and the stated edge cases.
The local ACL chain rule gives the stated weak derivatives, and the partition of unity patches them globally. The cited interfaces support the integrability and endpoint cases; no fatal defect found.
